People that played the game for 15 minutes and left a negative review because the game was "too simple" and "easy", should be banned from ever reviewing games. Let me start off by saying that this game is fantastic! I love the 80s-90s aesthetic of the game and the homage to Jackie Chan movies. It oozes with style and inspiration from such movies and I respect it. While the game is indeed somewhat easy compared to other games in the genre, it makes up for it with progression pacing. There's a ton on things to unlock! Every time you finish a level, you always get a minimum of 2 new things unlocked. Maybe now you can kick objects, or vault over obstacles, or even be able to enter areas now that you weren't able to in the beginning. The combo system is also something unique to the genre and it allows for a lot more build varieties, rather than always sticking to the same 5 or 6 best items like in other games. To finish off, while the game looks to be on the shorter side compared to its competitors, it makes up for it with it's price tag and the unique unlocks you get every time. This is a must pick for everyone that enjoys Survivor/Autoshooter games!

Very shallow survivor game. More about finding a good room to kite in a circle than it is about making a good build. One character. No evolutions like VS. It has melee weapons but they are underwhelming and usually less effective than your hands and feet. You're basically forced to pick a build that consists of all red or all blue attacks (look at the screenshots) because you get a huge damage bonus for each additional attack with the same color. You can't skip upgrades, you can only reroll once you unlock that option. Extremely limited enemy variety. The formula is: pick either all red or blue, get a few life regen rolls and some crit, then spend the rest of the level in one spot kiting in a circle and abusing objects you can use to separate yourself from the horde following you. Now they've added a couple extra difficulty levels but all it does is add annoying contact damage and nothing else. It just forces you to play in a much more tedious way that requires an insane level of microing (or geometry abuse) to avoid enemies while still hitting them with full combos. Imagine having to move away from a horde but then having to turn back to them every half second so your attack goes the right way, and then turning back the other way to keep moving before they catch up. You cannot walk one way and attack another. The game is also not visually impressive imo. All your attacks are punches and kicks or traditional melee weapons, so you have no crazy visual effects like other survivor games. I beat all the levels and after 4 hours I have no desire to keep playing. I did get at least $1 per hour of gameplay but I think I'd rather just have that time and money back. All these reviews that say the game is innovative or an "evolution" of the genre? Hard disagree.

Now to preface this negative review, this game is good, and worth the money. In most other situations I'd still be giving a thumbs up, but when comparing it to its genre, the survivors-like bullet heaven that's cheap as hell, it does fall short in the gameplay department. If you're looking for something to burn maybe 10 or 20 hours on and just kinda look at the visuals it's a good enough game. My chief problem comes in at the abilities and customization, or lack thereof. While the melee system is particular and robust and has some depth, it is all still short range melee attacks. In a genre that is often defined by its absurdly extravagant and explosive roster of unique weapons and abilities, this game only ever has punches and kicks and depending on build those attacks may shoot blue waves, do an AOE explosion looking thing, or some secret third thing since I haven't gotten enough yellow moves to see what their serial bonus is yet. The environmental gameplay does add some much needed spice, but only a small measure and it's not like you can specialize or customize those abilities per run. TLDR, there's only really one way to play karate survivor, and imo that's not very good when most other games in the genre are defined by their insane weapon/ability combos. If you're a casual gamer that just thinks it's a cool premise and sees 10-20 hours of gameplay as a fair trade for 5 bucks (it is) then you'll probably enjoy it, but to those that are deep in the survivors genre and used to throwing laser morning stars that explode into dark holes which procs twinned lighting strikes that spawn presents or something you probably want to give this one a pass.

游戏题材确实新颖，对得起价格的一个游戏，但个人觉得如果作者后续还打算更新的话需要注意几个方面 世界上最遥远的距离，不是是否刷老头的问题，而是老头在我面前，我没有穿刺攻击。 1. 我都成为传奇了，还没解锁墨西哥卷和手里剑 2. 连段特效也没有数值和效果说明，到现在不知道黄色连段干嘛用的（感谢留言） 3. 招式和特殊效果以及击退范围好歹出个关键字啊，就算有动画，我也不知道哪些是180，360，哪些是穿刺啊（后面发现卡片上有范围和推力，但推击是否是有推力的技能尚不清楚） 4. 一局游戏目前看起来能解锁的招式固定在8-12种左右，疑似伪随机，但又没有种子机制，毒种复盘都做不到 5. 基于以上原因，以及逆天的招式需要一个一个解锁，至今没用穿刺攻击打到疯汉 6. 腿功范围大，基础伤害高，击退效果强，范围收益加成明显，拳和追求连段反而成了小丑，建议出一个卡片能加强拳基础数值 7. 传奇最后两关数值感人。地铁BOSS我都能贴身硬吃伤害秒，地铁2人组一拳打掉我80血。更想不明白天台的刀墙都还在1W血以内，最后两关直接变成20W了，导致天台酒吧18分钟左右能75级左右，地铁20分钟通关只有50多级。 8. 强烈建议出的卡片：加敌人数量。 补充： 1. 反方向攻击和向下攻击简直是招式系统最大的败笔，实在要做建议加入一个玩家选项-自动选择攻击方向，点名批评不动如山，撼地和醉拳，新月和反踢，但向下攻击基本救不活了。 2. 连段中插入的莫名奇怪的攻击方式导致连段很难有效连，点名批评蝴蝶前的新月（又是你），大范围击退清影后的镰刀腿。 3. 玩完所有传奇后发现椅子是真好玩，但好像只存在与酒吧，但酒吧的强度和时间又有限，哎 基于以上原因，个人认为版本号不应该是1.0.X 而是应该 0.8-9.X。除非后续更新会很少

机制上与同类型游戏存在一定区分度，有独到的体验仿街机游戏的美术风格。但由于它存在的缺陷有些过于显眼，加上steam社区目前不存在中评，只能暂时给出差评了。 首先，想要模仿并强调上世纪80-90年代的港台动作片中角色对道具和环境的互动，这种想法确实很好，然而游戏中却很难体验到类似上述动作片的打戏应有的趣味性与刺激感。除了被动升级和部分随着流程推进而解锁的环境/物品交互技能外，就没有任何能够提升环境物品/武器/道具对敌人造成的伤害了，一场游戏初期的敌人或许尚能通过这些交互的手段进行直接击杀，但随着游戏流程的推进和游戏难度的提升，上述攻击方式对敌人所能造成的伤害将远逊于角色本身的搏击技所带来的伤害。像是高难度下在人堆中进行近战搏击时，倘若不慎捡起某项武器，那么这将导致玩家因输出/击退距离不够而瞬间大量扣血甚至暴毙。同样重要的一点是，除了直接的伤害外，敌人受环境交互/武器、道具攻击所能产生的影响，目前仅有晕眩、减速和流血debuff这几项属性上的效果，而无法做到像本作参考的对象那样有诸如摔倒、燃烧、战斗力减弱/丧失、盲目等多种多样的效果和与此相应的、充足的正向反馈。 其次，尽管游戏中设置了三种类型的近战技以凸显不同的build风格，但实际上性价比最高、杀伤力最直接且攻击范围最广泛的build，只有蓝色技能中的常见的大量腿技（典型如战车、空翻、弄清影等实用技能）。红色技能多为拳掌且攻击范围/伤害小，黄色技能攻击判定怪异且解锁条件较为苛刻，前中期流程中综合实用性均明显逊色于蓝色腿技，再加上目前仅有同色技能按数字顺序组合时才能增加技能伤害，这导致游玩本作的大部分时间里想要顺畅地进行通关，选择蓝色腿技进行正确的排列组合几乎是唯一解。除了build乏善可陈外，需要冷却时间的技能组合释放这一设计也略显别扭，加上前面提到的环境交互/武器道具伤害的乏力，由此导致实际战斗流程的大部分时候就变成了：走位等CD空窗期→进人堆释放技能→走位等CD的循环怪圈，这种体验反而是与本作所主打的环境互动背道而驰的。 此外，像是意味不明的技能解锁条件（看其他测评的反馈，貌似是BUG？），也很是让人头疼。一局游戏下来，玩家体验到的不是如《吸血鬼幸存者》那般通过经验积累所换来的、持续累积的正向反馈，而是时常可见的磕绊与愈发单调的乏味感，只能说本作目前仍存在着许多打磨和改进的空间。

这是我玩过的幸存者类游戏中的垫底作品，我甚至觉得我朋友做的同类型粗糙小游戏都比这部精加工的答辩要爽。唯一的亮点就是题材，细节零分。前期完全是在坐牢，莫名其妙的攻击范围，场景互动做的可以说玩下来绝大部分时候都是陷阱（打断连招），走着走着还经常会在觉得明明翻不过去的地方翻过去撞人吃伤害，而且还得在类幸存者中体验看发牌员心情？气的想砸键盘，各种升级的正反馈极差，还得靠局外成长，至于点满以后的体验如何，我不想知道，这两个小时的游玩中我没有得到任何快乐。
努力收集的卡，你根本用不上。解锁再多的动作，进去也就是固定的那几张，别想自己选一个想要的流派，卡组是硬塞给你，还有别看叫武林，不是国人产的游戏。很多动作设计的反人类，别想打到怪。

This is really more of a 'meh' than a 'nah' but I find it easier to give this a thumbs down than up. It shows a lot of promise, but this isn't some early access game that's receiving a ton of support, it's the full release and there's just not enough here for me to recommend. Everything great about the game starts to grow dull after you realize that's all there is about an hour or two in. I've still got some stuff to unlock, but given what I have to do to get there, I'm just not willing to put in the time. This game has so much unique stuff, but tries to coast by on that alone while ignoring a lot of what makes this genre of game fun to begin with. There's only one character, a small handful of upgrades, and the martial arts moves range from meh to nearly unusable. You could pretty easily see all this game has to offer in two hours.

The core problem is that "melee" does not work well with randomness; some moves (ie. weapons) have great damage and great range while some are the opposite. There's practically zero strategy involved if you want to get far, simply stay in the same position where enemies come from controlled directions (ie. have your back against a wall that can be jumped over / slide under) to farm experience and make your combo stronger. The game tries to give all sorts of incentives (objectives with rewards) to keep you moving, but it's less effective than camping on the same spot. The weapon items (temporary power-ups) are good in early game, but later they do less damage than your regular combos and since they are always automatically picked up when touched, they become actual hazards. However, the worst game design choice by far are the area bosses; they move slowly and have extremely telegraphed attacks, so unless you aren't sleeping they are a piece of cake. Overall it's a cheap game, but doesn't really hold up when compared to rivals in its own genre (like Vampire Survivors and Halls of Torment) which is kind of a shame considering its fresh theme and catchy audiovisual presentation.

Horribly balanced. The game isn't hard per se, but it depends almost entirely on RNG especially in the beginning when you don't have your stats upped yet. It's rng what skills you get, what color skills that you have to match for them to flow more optimally, etc. In the first let's say minute of a run the weapons you can pick up and use temporarily are useful, but after that, even with virtually no permanent upgrades yet, your skills own damage will outclass that of picked up weapons and they actually become a liability. Where your skills would quickly mow down a group of enemies, especially if you have 3 or more color matched in a row which gives an AoE effect, the picked up weapons just do relatively slow swings and only hit a small amount of enemies. If you don't have the health and/or regen to compensate, picking up a weapon can get you killed. You basically want to avoid them but unfortunately they're everywhere. End-game grind for completionists is absolute bs. The "rarest" achievements in the game are using a burrito and the shuriken. This is because the burrito only unlocks after 25 energy drink uses. At the time I beat the game on legend difficulty I had seen only 7 energy drinks. Not the worst grind, but definitely annoying. The real kicker is the shuriken. You have to get 5000 super weapon kills. I had done about 60 after I beat the entire game. Super weapon kills are kills with pistols, shotguns etc. Pistols consistently spawn on the map, the other stuff is rng. However, you'll only get 10-15 kills with the pistols per use and they don't respawn during a run. Also, since you can't aim manually, if you're lucky the game will aim into a large group of enemies and you'll get multiple kills, but usually it'll shoot the one lone guy that comes in walking from the edge of the screen ... The pistol won't even kill most enemies if you wait too long during a run to get it, but if you get it early the density of enemies is too low. So you're screwed either way. Organically you'd barely ever use it because it shoots in a single line obviously, and your own skills are AoE so they're always the superior option. Only way to reliably grind it out is to start a run on the first map, run for the storage room, get in, shoot the pistol, exit the map, repeat. The 5000 kills requirement is ludicrous.

Starts interesting, looks cool, but becomes too unfair and mechanically lacking. Dificulty ramps up too fast and most mechanics are useless from the start or become useless minutes into the game. You can unlock a dodge move that lets you wall climb, but its is useless and always moves you into an enemy. It requires you to stop attacking for a while, then you do a backflip and land a bit further away from the wall. By not attacking, enemies pile up even more and the distance isn't enough to clear the piled up enemies. The combo mechanic is interesting, but becomes a chore. You have 3 different types of attack, and each attack has a number. If you make a number sequence of the same color, the attacks get a bonus effect and bonus damage. The problem is, you can't take advantage of that due the randomness of the level ups. If your first attack is a red one, you will want more red ones to combo, but the game will almost always give you attacks from other types, or attacks with a number out of sequence. You get 3 rerolls per game at most and the move pool is massive. There is no way to think of a build and not using a combo is a sure loss due the lack of effectiveness. Also, you can't speed up attacks since there is no "fire rate" upgrade. The moves themselves are very bad. The range is ridiculously small, requiring you to basically touch the enemies (that cause contact damage!) Not only the moves are on a timer, most require you to face the enemy, so the gameplay consists of moving away from the enemy, then just before the combo starts, you turn around and hit them, and repeat the sequence. You can increase the range of the moves, but since the base range is already so small, the level ups might increase that range by a pixel. You can use some weapons and kick objects around, but they become too weak. You will get kills during the first few minutes, then the enemies will ramp so much they start to be a waste of time. Even the "super weapons" fall off like that. Upgrades not only are very random, they also have rarity tiers. So one "damage up" can be from 5% to 20% depending of your luck. Eventually, the game becomes very repetitive. You are fighting the same enemies, trying to get the same build and abusing the same mechanics to reach the boss (that are incredibly easy on some levels). Its cool for the novelty of a "Jackie Chan movie in a nutshell" game, but for the price, you are better getting Vampire Survivors for 1000x the content.

A simple and fun survivor game. If you like the genre and look of the game, it is well worth the 5 bucks. It is fluid to play and nicely polished. The pixel graphics are pleasantly and confidently executed. The twist to the survivor premise is pretty well executed also - you can interact a great deal with the environment, using nearby objects as weapons (though sometimes picking up a weapon can be a bad idea later in a level) and using obstacles to outmaneuver the waves of thugs. The game is pretty easy (I'm 14 hours in and have beaten the highest difficulty on most of the levels after a few tries) - you can build up meta buffs between attempts but each level and difficulty may take a few attempts. The bosses aren't a challenge - if you can survive the timer to summon them, you WILL beat the boss. After 14 hours I obviously haven't plumbed the depths of the game but it seems to not be that deep compared to Vampire Survivors, which to me is not a downside (VS is kind of cluttered now tbh). You can unlock lots of cool moves and more interactions with the environment as you play. When you first start learning the game and also at the start of each run, you will feel kind of weak and if you draw moves with "bad" hitboxes you will have a rough time - this is really the only significant challenging puzzle in game. Use the environment as much as possible during this phase as you build up your set of moves and improve them. Even the "bad" moves will work great late game if you upgrade them enough and put them in the proper combo order. Improving your attack range greatly mitigates the bad hitboxes. In the trendy genre of brain-dead dopamine games to play while watching youtube, this is a worthy entry with slightly more gameplay depth than some. It is fun and correctly priced.

Karate Survivor is a bullet heaven where the pitch is 80's action movie brawling with improvised weapons and environmental violence. And the game delivers with real conviction right up until you notice how few decisions it actually permits you to make. The animation deserves its praise first. Every punch, kick, and somersault is drawn with a level of detail that seems almost unreasonable for a 2D game at this price, and there are dozens of moves, all of them animated by someone who evidently cared. Environmental combat is equally strong. Slamming an enemy's face with a flying microwave and shoving a mop handle into approaching goons delivers as much satisfaction as a clean roundhouse kick, which is a genuinely impressive achievement. Positioning and timing carry real tactical weight, and when a run comes together you get to vault a table, throw a bottle at one thug, cave in a group's faces with a refrigerator door, and finish the last one with a tiger kick. Very few games let you choreograph a sequence that stupid and that satisfying. Now for the part where the design team wanders off. There is one character. That is not the starting roster, that IS the entire roster. Your opening move gets assigned to you by the game rather than chosen by you, which is a bold thing to withhold in a genre whose entire appeal is deciding what kind of monster you want to become this run. Everything offered afterward tends to complement whatever the game unilaterally decided you were, so those hundred-odd unlockable techniques quietly resolve into maybe four or five combos anyone would seriously run. You are not building anything. You're just following a script. The RNG makes this considerably worse. Rerolls are miserly and cannot be purchased with any currency, which means a run that refuses to offer you anything useful stays that way, and you get to sit through the rest of it knowing exactly how it ends. Someone made a game that hinges entirely on the draw and then decided the player should have almost no influence over the draw. Bold. For what it's worth, one can sum it up as a flashy take on the formula with no build variety whatsoever. Turns out the excellent animation was doing a lot of heavy lifting. But I'm still a sucker for Jackie Chan movies. A hundred moves, one build. Barely passing. 5/10
